# Full Results for All Eight User Simulators

This file is the complete version of the new-domain table in rebuttal W2, and provides the confidence intervals and significance tests requested in W3.

**Experimental setup.** Agent: Qwen3-14B, initialized from the same checkpoint and updated in a unified reinforcement learning framework using full multi-turn trajectories generated by each simulator.

- **τ²-bench**: 3 random training seeds (42 / 1234 / 2026); each checkpoint is evaluated on Retail (40 held-out test tasks) and Airline (20 held-out test tasks) with a GPT-4o user, 10 trials per task. The initial agent has no training randomness; its variation comes from three independent evaluations of the same checkpoint.
- **Proprietary dataset**: consistent with the evaluation protocol in the paper — each method is trained once, and each of the 168 test tasks is completed in three rounds of interaction by real humans. Every evaluation round requires human participation (504 human sessions per method), so the cost cannot support 10 trials per task as on τ²-bench; the table reports the mean ± sample standard deviation of accuracy over the three rounds, with means identical to Table 1 in the paper.

pass^1 is the average task success rate; pass^4 uses the τ-bench combinatorial unbiased estimator: for a task with c successes out of 10 trials, take \(\binom{c}{4}/\binom{10}{4}\), then average over tasks, measuring stability under repeated interactions; tool success rate is the proportion of required tool calls that are executed correctly. All numbers are percentages. Best in each column in bold.

## Proprietary Dataset: Confidence Intervals and Significance

95% confidence intervals are computed with the t distribution (n = 3 rounds, 2 degrees of freedom); p values are from two-sided Welch t tests between SimTeacher and each method.

| User simulator | Accuracy | 95% CI | SimTeacher lead | p value |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| — (initial agent) | 55.4±1.8 | [50.9, 59.9] | +29.3 | <0.001 |
| Qwen3-235B | 65.1±2.1 | [59.9, 70.3] | +19.6 | <0.001 |
| Gemini-2.5 | 63.3±1.7 | [59.1, 67.5] | +21.4 | <0.001 |
| DeepSeek-R1 | 66.5±1.9 | [61.8, 71.2] | +18.2 | <0.001 |
| USP-8B | 58.1±2.5 | [51.9, 64.3] | +26.6 | <0.001 |
| SEAD | 71.0±2.4 | [65.0, 77.0] | +13.7 | 0.002 |
| SFT SimTeacher | 75.6±2.1 | [70.4, 80.8] | +9.1 | 0.005 |
| SimTeacher | 84.7±1.5 | [81.0, 88.4] | — | — |

SimTeacher's confidence interval does not overlap with that of any other method.

## Interpretation Notes

- SimTeacher has the best mean on six of the seven metrics. Its Airline tool success rate is 0.5 points below SEAD's (not significant): tool success rate measures whether individual required tool operations are executed correctly, while pass^4 measures reliable end-to-end completion under repeated interactions — the two need not move in the same direction.
- In both domains, SimTeacher's pass^4 lead over SEAD (Retail +2.9, Airline +3.8) exceeds its pass^1 lead (+1.3, +3.3), suggesting that the gains show up not only in average success rate but also in reliability under repeated interactions.

## Conclusion

On the main result the reviewer cares about (the proprietary dataset), SimTeacher leads the strongest baseline SEAD by 13.7 points (p = 0.002) and leads SFT SimTeacher — same initialization but no BMG training — by 9.1 points (p = 0.005), with confidence intervals that do not overlap with any baseline. On the two public domains, SimTeacher has the highest mean on six of seven metrics, with the direction consistent across the three training seeds.
